title: Global Health Hazards From Human‐Derived Volatile Organic Compounds Amid Emission Variability
abstract: Health risks from high air pollution exposure remain challenging despite pollution control strategies. Health hazards caused by particulate matter and ozone have been reported for the past three decades. Here, we report the hazard quotient for Volatile Organic Compounds (VOCs) causing non‐carcinogenic risk globally using chemistry‐climate model simulations. We report hazard quotient (HQ) for three scenarios: (a) baseline scenario, (b) continued increasing emissions leading to doubling of anthropogenic VOCs (DVOCS), and (c) mitigation scenarios where emissions are reduced to half (HalfVOCS). Interestingly, we report that long‐term ambient exposure to VOCs increases non‐carcinogenic health risk by up to 36% in the high‐emission scenario. Hazardous VOCs such as benzene, formaldehyde, hydrogen cyanide, and acetonitrile remain at levels that pose chronic risks to large populations. Benzene and formaldehyde pose the greatest hazards, with maximum HQ ranging from 1.4 to 2.0. Additionally, the DVOCS scenario increases the risk to the exposed population by 18.6%–21.5% in northern India and eastern China, and by 10.7% in West‐Central Africa. Conversely, the HalfVOCS scenario shows a decrease in the exposed population of −3 to −21%. We estimate that approximately a million people face chronic respiratory and neurological risks from current ambient VOCs levels. Our findings demonstrate that VOCs exposure constitutes a major driver of the global disease burden, necessitating immediate international emission‐reduction strategies.

title: Thermally programmed disassembly and reconstruction of 2D polymer platelets via melting-governed crystallization-driven self-assembly
abstract:
‘Crystallization-driven self-assembly is a useful tool for the synthesis of polymer nanostructures with precise dimensions, but the melting behavior of polymer crystals grown in solution has remained largely unexplored. Here, the authors show that melting temperature is a structurally sensitive descriptor and an active design parameter for 2D platelets.’ 
 Crystallization-driven self-assembly (CDSA) has emerged as a powerful methodology to precisely control the morphology and size of polymer nanostructures, enabling the formation of 1D and 2D nanomaterials. Yet, the melting behavior of polymer crystals grown in solution using this technique has remained largely unexplored. Here, we show that melting temperature is a structurally sensitive descriptor and an active design parameter for 2D poly(ε-caprolactone) platelets formed by seeded living CDSA. Using nano differential scanning calorimetry, we establish quantitative thickness-melting correlations consistent with Gibbs-Thomson theory for finite, solution-grown lamellae. Leveraging these insights, we engineer multilayer platelets with programmed thermal stability gradients that undergo rapid, selective disassembly under mild conditions (37 °C), yielding uniform hollow architectures within minutes. Upon cooling, released polymer chains undergo spatially confined recrystallization, allowing reversible reconstruction and self-healing of the platelet framework. This work establishes melting as a powerful thermodynamic handle for probing and reconfiguring CDSA-derived nanostructures in solution. ‘Crystallization-driven self-assembly is a useful tool for the synthesis of polymer nanostructures with precise dimensions, but the melting behavior of polymer crystals grown in solution has remained largely unexplored. Here, the authors show that melting temperature is a structurally sensitive descriptor and an active design parameter for 2D platelets.’

title: Sustainability cost of defect engineering in color centers for quantum communications
abstract:
Sustainable manufacturing is becoming an increasingly important consideration for emerging quantum technologies. Here, the authors assess the environmental, chemical, human-health, and economic impacts of defect engineering strategies for color-center platforms used in quantum communications, highlighting trade-offs between quantum functionality and resource demands while identifying lower-impact solutions. 
 Quantum communication relies on optically active color centers for scalable spin-photon networking, yet the sustainability implications of defect engineering remain largely unexplored. We comparatively evaluate twenty host crystal-defect generation combinations across diamond, SiC, h-BN, GaN, ZnO using ion implantation, e-beam irradiation, laser writing, and heteroepitaxial growth techniques. A multi-attribute cradle-to-gate framework integrating life cycle, chemical hazard, human health toxicity, and technoeconomic assessments reveals distinct thermodynamic, chemical, health, and economic tradeoffs emerge across defect engineering pathways. h-BN paired with laser writing shows the lowest overall burdens, with low energy demand, global warming potential <20 kg CO2 eq./chip, minimal hazard/toxicity profiles, and lowest fabrication cost. SiC provides a balanced near-term pathway by retaining strong quantum functionality while moderating sustainability burdens. ZnO and GaN show selective process-level advantages for integrated photonics, whereas diamond remains burden-intensive due to energy-demanding growth and complex post-defect stabilization requirements. Identified greener interventions enable scalable and resource-conscious quantum communication hardware. Sustainable manufacturing is becoming an increasingly important consideration for emerging quantum technologies. Here, the authors assess the environmental, chemical, human-health, and economic impacts of defect engineering strategies for color-center platforms used in quantum communications, highlighting trade-offs between quantum functionality and resource demands while identifying lower-impact solutions.

title: Bulk mesophases modeling of ferroelectric nematic liquid crystals
abstract:
Ferroelectric nematic liquid crystals are an emerging class of materials in which nematic orientational order coexists with spontaneous macroscopic polarization. Vats et al. develop a free-energy framework to rationalize their bulk structures and predict potential bend-instability-driven mesophases. 
 Ferroelectric nematic liquid crystals (FNLCs) are emerging materials that combine orientational order with spontaneous macroscopic polarization. They exhibit distinctive properties, such as polar domain formation, field-tunable textures, and strong electro-elastic couplings. However, due to the complexity of the underlying mechanisms, the bulk structure of the emergent mesophases is not yet fully understood, and a generalized description of all observed phases is still lacking. Here, we demonstrate the bulk mesophases of FNLCs as stabilized by a combination of flexoelectricity, elasticity, bulk ordering, and polarization-nematic couplings. Specifically, we develop Landau de-Gennes-like free energy framework that predicts and explains the structure of major experimentally observed ferroelectric nematic phases, including ferroelectric nematic, antiferroelectric splay nematic, apolar nematic, and isotropic phase, notably together with the correct phase transition sequences. Additionally, we predict the possible existence of new bend-instability-driven mesophase characterized by periodic splay-bend structure. Finally, we calculate a complete phase diagram of bulk ferroelectric nematics as dependent on the key coupling mechanisms, which could possibly enable the predictive design and applications of these novel emergent ferroelectric nematic materials. Ferroelectric nematic liquid crystals are an emerging class of materials in which nematic orientational order coexists with spontaneous macroscopic polarization. Vats et al. develop a free-energy framework to rationalize their bulk structures and predict potential bend-instability-driven mesophases.

title: Near-atomistic simulations reveal the molecular principles that control chromatin structure and phase separation
abstract:
Russell et al. introduce a 10 × faster, chemically detailed chromatin model bridging molecular and genomic scales, revealing how DNA sequence, spacing and histone acetylation govern chromatin folding and phase separation. 
 Understanding how chromatin’s physicochemical properties shape its emergent organization is central to deciphering genome function. To address this, we present OpenCGChromatin, a high-performance coarse-grained model that achieves near-atomistic simulations of chromatin systems an order of magnitude larger than previously possible, spanning biomolecular condensates and fibers tens of kilobases in length. OpenCGChromatin simulations independently predict, from physicochemical principles, the linker-DNA-dependent chromatin structures observed by cryo-ET and the relative thermodynamic stability of condensates inferred from biochemical assays. Crucially, OpenCGChromatin resolves histone-tail dynamics and interaction networks that remain inaccessible experimentally, explaining how linker-DNA length controls histone tail accessibility and the resulting multiscale structure of chromatin condensates. Extending simulations to 108-nucleosome fibers shows that acetylation disrupts chromatin compaction in a pattern-specific manner by weakening key tail-mediated interactions, with H4K16 and H3K9 emerging as the most energetically disruptive modifications. These results position OpenCGChromatin as a powerful framework for linking molecular detail to emergent chromatin organization. Russell et al. introduce a 10 × faster, chemically detailed chromatin model bridging molecular and genomic scales, revealing how DNA sequence, spacing and histone acetylation govern chromatin folding and phase separation.

title: Monolithic three-dimensionally integrated memristor-thin-film transistor for electrically programmable multimode reservoir computing
abstract:
Current reservoir computing hardware is efficient but limited by fixed dynamics. Shim et al. report a monolithically integrated memristor-transistor reservoir with electrically programmable temporal dynamics, supporting multiple temporal processing modes for motion recognition and biomedical signal classification. 
 Reservoir computing offers an efficient framework for processing temporal information, but most hardware reservoirs exhibit fixed or narrowly tunable dynamics determined by intrinsic material relaxation time. A monolithically integrated memristor-thin-film transistor reservoir kernel of this study enables electrically programmable temporal dynamics across a wide timescale. By vertically and monolithically integrating Ru/HfO2/TiN memristors with In2O3 channel thin-film transistors (TFTs), the memristive conductance dynamics are modulated by the TFTs. The temporal response can be actively tuned over three orders of magnitude experimentally and extended to over eight orders of magnitude via circuit configuration, demonstrating temporally unconstrained hardware with general applicability for spatiotemporal data processing. Implemented as an active reservoir array compatible with back-end-of-line integration, the system exhibits reliable spatiotemporal responses. The system demonstrates spatiotemporal computing capability through dynamic motion recognition in vision sensors and ultrasound signal classification, achieving high accuracy with a simple linear readout layer. Current reservoir computing hardware is efficient but limited by fixed dynamics. Shim et al. report a monolithically integrated memristor-transistor reservoir with electrically programmable temporal dynamics, supporting multiple temporal processing modes for motion recognition and biomedical signal classification.

title: Top-down semantic predictions align phonetic neuronal dynamics in human superior temporal gyrus
abstract:
How semantic information influences phonetic processing during speech perception remains unclear. Here, the authors show that semantic predictions reshape phonetic representations in human temporal cortex at the level of neuronal population activity. 
 Speech processing involves a hierarchy of cognitive layers from low-level phonetic to high-level semantic representations. However, interactions are not only feed-forward; feedback mechanisms are crucial for real-time, accurate speech recognition. Yet how distant levels interface during speech processing remains unclear. Here, we analyzed intracortical recordings from 624 neurons across three human participants implanted with microelectrode arrays in the anterior superior temporal gyrus during an auditory semantic categorization task and natural speech perception. We identified distinct neural subspaces, or manifolds, for lexico-semantic and phonetic features, with a functional separation of the corresponding low-dimensional dynamics. We contrasted a bottom-up cumulative and a top-down semantic hypothesis on phonetic-semantic temporal alignment, and found phonetic alignment to word-level semantic representations, signaling top-down prediction. These effects were consistent across participants at the spiking level, and remained undetected in adjacent ECoG recordings. These findings demonstrate the reorganization of neuronal population dynamics supporting phonetic representations during semantic prediction. How semantic information influences phonetic processing during speech perception remains unclear. Here, the authors show that semantic predictions reshape phonetic representations in human temporal cortex at the level of neuronal population activity.

title: DCAF7 regulates hematopoietic stem cell function and differentiation through polycomb repressive complex 1 modulation
abstract:
This study identifies DCAF7 as a new regulator of blood stem cells showing how it controls chromatin to preserve stem cell function with implications for understanding normal and malignant blood formation. 
 DCAF7 is one of the few DCAFs expressed in hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs). Using a conditional knockout mouse model, we discovered that the absence of DCAF7 leads to accumulation of differentiating progenitors in the bone marrow, and impairs self-renewal capacity of HSCs upon transplantation. Furthermore, loss of Dcaf7 accelerates the differentiation of HSCs into the myeloid lineage. At the molecular level, DCAF7 interacts with components of the polycomb repressive complex 1 (PRC1) and promotes their assembly into large macromolecular complexes. Chromatin profiling revealed that loss of DCAF7 leads to increased localization of RING1B at transcriptionally active genomic loci. This increased binding was observed at genes involved in myeloid differentiation and was associated with increased mRNA expression. Lastly, inhibition of KDM2/7 proteins rescues the defective growth of Dcaf7 null HSCs in vitro. Together, these data reveal that DCAF7 is a novel regulator of the PRC1 complex and epigenetic enzymes that control HSC differentiation. This study identifies DCAF7 as a new regulator of blood stem cells showing how it controls chromatin to preserve stem cell function with implications for understanding normal and malignant blood formation.

title: Seasonal predictability of spring solar resources and wind-solar variability across the United States
abstract:
Spring solar resources can be reliably predicted across the United States Southwest, with skillful wind-solar variability forecasts and key climate drivers identified, according to a state-of-the-art seasonal forecast system and predictability analysis. 
 The rapid expansion of solar and wind energy across the United States is increasing the demand for reliable seasonal forecasts to guide energy planning and grid operations. Here we show high seasonal prediction skill for springtime solar energy resources over the southwestern United States using a state-of-the-art seasonal forecast system. We identify two leading sources of solar predictability: a dominant component linked to primary El Niño-Southern Oscillation conditions, and a secondary component associated with El Niño-Southern Oscillation diversity and tropical Atlantic variability. Together, these components explain the spatial structure of forecast skill and its underlying physical drivers. State-level evaluations show robust solar prediction skill in high-resource states. The forecast system also captures the compound behavior of wind-solar variability and historical co-fluctuations associated with seasonal energy droughts and surpluses. These results provide a physically interpretable foundation for integrating seasonal forecasts into wind-solar energy planning and compound risk management. Spring solar resources can be reliably predicted across the United States Southwest, with skillful wind-solar variability forecasts and key climate drivers identified, according to a state-of-the-art seasonal forecast system and predictability analysis.

title: Future methane measurement campaigns require basin-specific sampling strategies
abstract:
The presence of super-emitters in oil and gas basins can influence sample size requirements when estimating methane emissions, according to data analyses from six US oil and gas basins. 
 Methane emissions from the oil and gas sector follow right-skewed, heavy-tailed distributions, making it hard to accurately quantify average emissions with a limited number of measurements. In this study, we probe the statistical implications of sampling (i.e., measuring) from these right-skewed, heavy-tailed distributions using six US oil and gas basins as an example. For each basin, we provide a minimum sample size that bounds error in the average emission rate estimate introduced by sampling variability. We find that the largest emissions drive sample behavior, and by extension, sample size requirements; samples will underestimate (overestimate) average emissions if super-emitters are observed below (above) their true frequency. Importantly, we show that very large sample sizes can be necessary to mitigate this sampling effect. Furthermore, we find that a one-size-fits-all sampling strategy across basins is suboptimal; differences in super-emitter characteristics between basins necessitate a more tailored sampling approach. The presence of super-emitters in oil and gas basins can influence sample size requirements when estimating methane emissions, according to data analyses from six US oil and gas basins.

title: Aridity-driven shifts in plant–microbial diversity relationships across the arid and semi-arid grasslands of northern China
abstract:
Increasing aridity drives taxon-specific biodiversity thresholds in northern Chinese grasslands, reducing plant, bacterial, and fungal diversity while increasing archaeal species diversity and restructuring plant-microbe coupling, based on a field survey across arid and semi-arid regions. 
 Climate change-driven aridification threatens above- and belowground biodiversity, yet how the relationships between plant diversity and soil microbial diversity change along aridity gradients remains unclear. Here, we conducted a 4,000-km field survey across arid and semi-arid grasslands in northern China. We show that soil conditions, plant diversity, and microbial diversity exhibit sequential threshold responses along the aridity gradient. Beyond these thresholds, plant, bacterial, and fungal diversity generally decline, whereas archaeal species diversity increases. As aridity increases, the negative effects of soil salinity on plant, bacterial, and fungal diversity become stronger, whereas soil salinity shows increasingly positive associations with archaeal species diversity. Plant–bacteria and plant–fungi diversity relationships strengthen in drier regions, whereas plant–archaea relationships become decoupled. These findings show that aridity acts as a strong environmental filter, selecting stress-tolerant species and restructuring plant–microbial diversity coupling in a taxon-specific manner, and highlight the importance of aridity-dependent biodiversity coupling for shaping ecosystem resilience in arid and semi-arid grasslands under ongoing aridification. Increasing aridity drives taxon-specific biodiversity thresholds in northern Chinese grasslands, reducing plant, bacterial, and fungal diversity while increasing archaeal species diversity and restructuring plant-microbe coupling, based on a field survey across arid and semi-arid regions.

authors: Zhansen Zhang;Yu Li;Yuxin Zhang;Simin Peng;Mingjun Gao
title: Strong latitudinal contrasts in global wet/dry patterns since the Last Glacial Maximum and under future warming
abstract:
Global wet and dry changes since the Last Glacial Maximum reveal strong latitudinal contrasts as shown by model simulation and lake-level records; future warming will exacerbate the spread of arid zones and the global wet and dry differentiation will expand. 
 Understanding regional wetting and drying under global warming remains challenging. Here we show, using global climate simulations and 191 records of past climate, that terrestrial moisture changes over the past 21,000 years follow a pronounced latitudinal pattern. Our reconstruction shows progressive wetting at high northern latitudes from the Last Glacial Maximum to the pre-industrial period. By contrast, many regions dominated by mid-latitude westerly winds are wetter during cold periods, whereas low-latitude monsoon regions are generally wetter during warm periods. These contrasts arise from seasonal changes in precipitation and evaporation and shifts in atmospheric circulation caused by changing ice sheets, greenhouse gas concentrations, and incoming solar radiation. A similar latitude-dependent structure appears in modern observations. Future simulations project drying across many subtropical and mid-latitude regions, but wetting at high latitudes and in monsoon regions. Continued warming is therefore likely to strengthen global differences between drying and wetting regions and expand water stress in vulnerable drylands. Global wet and dry changes since the Last Glacial Maximum reveal strong latitudinal contrasts as shown by model simulation and lake-level records; future warming will exacerbate the spread of arid zones and the global wet and dry differentiation will expand.

title: Long-term, national-scale records of landslide persistence and dynamic hazard in a mountain landscape
abstract:
Pre-existing, persistent landslides dominate landslide hazard in Nepal, accounting for about 80% of visible landslides each year, highlighting the need to explicitly incorporate existing landslides into future hazard assessments, according to analysis of a 22-year time-stack of landslide occurrence. 
 As mountain populations grow and exposure to hazard increases, understanding the dynamic hazard posed by landslides is essential. However, our ability to constrain landslide hazard is limited by relatively few good-quality datasets that are often collected across small geographical areas. These datasets typically focus on specific triggering events, such as earthquakes or rainstorms, further complicating assessments of landslide hazard through time. To better capture landslide hazard through space and time, long-term datasets over large extents are needed. Here, we analyse a 22-year record of landslide occurrence to decipher the dynamic nature of the hazard posed by landslides in Nepal. We find that recurrent or persistent landslides dominate national-scale patterns of landsliding, accounting for c. 80% of all visible landslides at any given point in time. Of new landslide areas, only half occurred in locations >30 m away from other landslides. These findings emphasise the importance of also considering pre-existing landslides when assessing hazard. Individual triggering events, including both earthquakes and rainfall, leave a distinctive footprint visible at the national scale in metrics such as landslide density, persistence, and recurrence. Such metrics add significant value to multi-temporal landslide inventories and provide a basis for mitigation efforts, particularly where resources are limited. Pre-existing, persistent landslides dominate landslide hazard in Nepal, accounting for about 80% of visible landslides each year, highlighting the need to explicitly incorporate existing landslides into future hazard assessments, according to analysis of a 22-year time-stack of landslide occurrence.

title: Coupled Sb-Hg isotopes reveal mixed basement and deeply recycled mantle-related metal sources for the South China antimony belt
abstract:
Coupled Sb-Hg isotope signatures from the South China antimony belt reveal that ore metals were sourced from both Precambrian basement rocks and a deep recycled mantle reservoir, demonstrating the utility of coupled Sb-Hg isotopes for tracing metal provenance, according to coupled Sb and Hg isotope analyses. 
 Understanding the sources of metals in hydrothermal ore systems is fundamental for improving exploration models. However, direct tracers of metal sources remain limited, especially for large, low-temperature deposits. Here we apply coupled antimony (Sb) and mercury (Hg) isotope analyses to Sb deposits from South China, the World’s largest antimony metallogenic province. The dataset reveals substantial variability in δ123Sb (−0.64 to +0.69‰), δ202Hg (−1.86 to +2.08‰), and Δ199Hg (−0.20 to +0.14‰). These data support a model involving two metal sources, namely a deep, recycled mantle-related reservoir and Precambrian basement metamorphic rocks. Our results demonstrate that coupled Sb and Hg isotopes provide a potentially powerful tool with which to identify the metal sources for Sb ore deposits, and that their application may help refine models for these deposits globally and help decode the dynamic interplay between Earth’s interior and crustal metal cycling. Coupled Sb-Hg isotope signatures from the South China antimony belt reveal that ore metals were sourced from both Precambrian basement rocks and a deep recycled mantle reservoir, demonstrating the utility of coupled Sb-Hg isotopes for tracing metal provenance, according to coupled Sb and Hg isotope analyses.

title: Lake eutrophication increases unprotected organic carbon pools in sediments
abstract:
The long-term carbon-burial capacity of lakes globally is reduced by eutrophication by lowering reactive iron oxide-bound organic carbon and increasing unprotected organic carbon pools in sediments, according to global lake assessments, field observations, and incubation experiments. 
 Reactive iron oxide-bound organic carbon (Fe–OC) is a key pathway for long-term carbon burial, but its effectiveness under increasingly widespread eutrophication remains uncertain. Here we show that Fe–OC accounts for 16% of total organic carbon and buries at ~14 Mt C yr−1 in lakes globally, equivalent to ~27% of the marine Fe–OC sink despite lakes covering only ~1.25% of marine area. However, bloom-prone lakes exhibit lower Fe–OC content and contribution to sedimentary organic carbon than non–bloom-prone lakes. Field observations and incubation experiments further reveal that bloom-induced redox fluctuations and low-aromaticity algal organic matter inputs jointly accelerate Fe–OC turnover and reduce organic carbon loading on Fe minerals, causing Fe–OC losses of up to ~68%. These findings suggest that eutrophication weakens the long-term carbon burial capacity of lakes by increasing unprotected organic carbon pools in sediments, necessitating reevaluation of their contributions to the global carbon budget. The long-term carbon-burial capacity of lakes globally is reduced by eutrophication by lowering reactive iron oxide-bound organic carbon and increasing unprotected organic carbon pools in sediments, according to global lake assessments, field observations, and incubation experiments.
